title: Minimum Removals to Balance Array
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the minimum number of elements that need to be removed so that the remaining array is balanced.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the minimum number of elements that need to be removed so that the remaining array is balanced. An array is balanced if the maximum element in the array is no greater than k times the minimum element. Note that an array with a single element is always considered balanced.
constraints: A nonempty remainder is balanced when max <= k*min.
hints: After sorting, every maximum-size balanced selection can be taken as one contiguous value window.
Fix each minimum and binary-search the last value no greater than k times it.
Maximize the inclusive window length and remove everything else.
Any skipped in-range value can be added without changing the extremes, so an optimal subset is contiguous in sorted order.
editorial: Any skipped in-range value can be added without changing the extremes, so an optimal subset is contiguous in sorted order.

The largest balanced subset has two elements, so remove two.
